narrative:
The model estimated a 56.8% chance that you would fail the bar exam on the first attempt. That is a slightly-more-likely-than-not risk, and it is why your law school application was denied: the decision treated that estimated risk as too high for admission.

The strongest factor was your third-year class rank. You were in the second decile, while accepted students averaged around the sixth decile; this low relative standing pushed the prediction toward bar failure more than any other factor. The second most influential factor was your undergraduate GPA of 3.20, just below the accepted-student average of 3.23. Compared with the rest of your profile, this slightly lowered the estimated risk, but it was not strong enough to offset the other concerns. The third factor was your first-year class rank, also second decile versus an accepted average near the sixth decile, which again pushed toward failure.

This is a risk estimate, not a certainty. To improve a future application, focus on strengthening the academic signals that raised concern: discuss the reasons behind your low class ranks with an advisor, take steps to show improved academic performance, consider retaking the LSAT because your 35 is below the accepted average of about 37, and seek programs that review your full record and any contextual challenges.
